To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a novel class of PhotoCORMs that can be used for the detection of CO release in vitro.

five novel photoactivatable manganese(I) tris-carbonyl compounds based on the tris(pyrazolylmethyl)amine (tpma) ligand scaffold were synthesized and fully structurally and spectroscopically characterized.

five new photoactivatable CO releasing manganese(I) tris-carbonyl complexes were prepared and characterized and their CO release properties were investigated by IR spectroscopy, and their in vitro CO releasing properties were investigated by fluorescence microscopy using COP-1.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of novel PhotoCORMs based on manganese(i) tris-carbonyl complexes with the aim of providing an improved understanding of the photophysical and photochemical properties of these compounds, which may serve as a basis for the design and development of future PhotoCORMs.
a new class of photoactivatable CO releasing molecules (PhotoCorms).
the design and synthesis of novel manganese(I) tris-carbonyl PhotoCORMs and their in vitro evaluation as potential CO-releasing agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CO-release from the complexes was found to be dependent on the electronic structure of the ligands.

the CO-release properties of the compounds can be tuned by the nature of the imine/amino group in the ligand, and that the presence of a phenyl substituent with an electron-donating or electron-withdrawing group has no influence.

the presence of an imine group in the bpea-based ligands leads to a higher CO-release quantum yield and a more efficient CO-releasing process, which is in line with the results obtained from the DFT/TDDFT calculations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed new manganese(i) tris-carbonyl PhotoCORMs based on a tridentate bis(3-pyrazolyl)ethylenediamine (bpea(NH)2) backbone with pendant phenyl rings substituted at 4-positions with various functional groups.

the presence of the imine group in the bpea-based ligands has a strong influence on the electronic structure of the complexes, resulting in a significant decrease of the HOMO-LUMO energy gap, which is reflected in the photophysical behavior of the complexes.
a new series of photoactive CO-releasing molecules has been designed and synthesized based on the tricarbonylmanganese(i) core.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a simple modification of the bpea backbone with a 4-substituent on the pendant phenyl ring allows for a modulation of the photophysical behavior of the complexes, and the resulting compounds can act as photoactivatable CO releasing molecules.

a simple change of the substituents at the phenyl ring can have a dramatic influence on the photophysical behavior of the complexes, and that the presence of the amine functionality is crucial for the photoactivity.
the bpea-based manganese(I) tris-carbonyl complexes are promising PhotoCORMs with potential applications in cell biology.
